s: Automatic call limiter that detects downstream failures and stops hammering a broken service to allow recovery.
w: Tracks failure rate (or latency) of calls to a dependency over a rolling window. When failures exceed a threshold, the breaker trips into OPEN state: calls fail-fast immediately without network cost. After a cooldown, a probe (HALF-OPEN) tests if the dependency recovered; success closes the breaker, failure reopens it. This prevents cascade failure and gives the downstream time to heal.
use: Calls to external/third-party APIs with unpredictable availability
Inter-service RPC where one failing service should not cascade to the whole mesh
Database failover scenarios where the new primary needs seconds to stabilize
Any call path where retry storms will worsen an already degraded dependency
avoid: Dependencies that must always be called regardless of state (auth checks with no fallback)
Replacing retry logic entirely - circuit breaker stops calls, retries handle transient failures

props.failure_threshold_pct: Failure rate that trips the breaker (default 50%)
props.cooldown_ms: How long OPEN before probing HALF-OPEN

pat.d: When breaker is open, serve cached/default/degraded data instead of error.

pits: Too-sensitive thresholds tripping on transient blips - tune failure window and volume minimum
No monitoring on breaker state changes - log and alert on OPEN transitions
Forgetting to implement fallback behavior - open breaker with no fallback is just a different error
tips: Three-state model (CLOSED/OPEN/HALF-OPEN) is the expected answer - name all three
Pair with retry: circuit breaker prevents retries against a known-bad dependency
